---
title: "Windows line endings make a check fail on Linux"
ref: ENV-04
categories: [OS and CI]
impact: cryptique
attendu: "the same check as on Windows"
versions: "All"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2019, 2021)"
---

::: {.piege .piege-statique}
```bash
git config core.autocrlf false  # on the Windows machine: CRLF files are committed as is
git push
# then, in the Linux CI
Rscript -e 'rcmdcheck::rcmdcheck()'
```

```text
input string 1 is invalid in this locale
```
:::

This pitfall depends on git, two operating systems and a CI, so it cannot be replayed in the browser.

## Why

Windows ends lines with two characters, carriage return then line feed (`\r\n`), Linux and macOS with a single one (`\n`). Depending on the git configuration, files can reach the repository or the CI with extra `\r` characters.

These invisible characters end up in `DESCRIPTION`, in data files or in the code, and make tools that read the text fail. The original incident ended with an error along the lines of "input string 1 is invalid in this locale", which hints at encoding rather than line endings.

## The fix

Set the line endings in the repository itself, through a `.gitattributes` file, rather than in each machine's configuration.

::: {.piege .piege-statique}
```text
# .gitattributes
* text=auto eol=lf
*.R text eol=lf
DESCRIPTION text eol=lf
```
:::
